definition: Sensory overload is a state in which sensory input, especially in unpredictable healthcare environments, becomes too much to manage. In autistic people, it is linked with heightened stress, anxiety, and avoidant behaviour.

reasons: The packet does not provide a definition of “sensory overload” (e.g., it does not state that sensory input becomes “too much to manage”), so the core definitional claim is unsupported.

The definition specifies a “diagnosis” framing, but the packet presents sensory overload as a barrier in healthcare settings and a factor in study aims, not as a diagnostic construct with diagnostic criteria or diagnostic usage.

The claim that sensory overload is “especially” in unpredictable healthcare environments is only partially supported: the packet mentions unpredictable built environments in healthcare settings, but does not explicitly define sensory overload as being “especially” tied to unpredictability in healthcare environments in general.

The autism-specific linkage is only partially supported in the packet: it states that divergent sensory processing and unpredictable built environments can exacerbate stress-induced anxiety and avoidant behaviour, but the definition asserts this is “linked with” sensory overload itself (the packet does not clearly establish sensory overload as the direct mediator of those outcomes.
